definitions.definition: The lack of own-being (svabhāva) of all dharmas — persons, aggregates, the path and nirvāṇa alike; not nothingness and not an entity: 'form is emptiness, emptiness is form'. Emptiness does not make dharmas empty; they are empty. It is to be realized without being grasped as a view.
The tathāgatagarbha is empty of the adventitious, separable defilements and not empty of the inseparable buddha-qualities; emptiness misread as mere absence is criticized.

equivalents.note: Pali suññatā (U36): in the Nikāyas emptiness of self; the Mahāyāna extends it to all dharmas

definitions.definition: The sixth perfection: wisdom that apprehends no dharma, not even itself; the 'mother of the buddhas' and leader of the other five perfections; also the name of the sūtras that teach it and, personified, a goddess.

literal: perfection of wisdom; wisdom gone beyond

cross_language.form: shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa
banruo boluomi(duo) 般若波羅蜜(多)

definitions.definition: The way things really are, unaltered: the suchness of the Tathāgata and of all dharmas is one undivided suchness; 'Tathāgata' is a synonym of true suchness.
Suchness with stains (samalā tathatā) is the tathāgatagarbha, suchness without stains the dharmakāya; in the Awakening of Faith 'mind as suchness' is the one mind's unborn aspect.

The limit of reality, synonym of emptiness and suchness; to 'realize the reality-limit' is to enter final peace, which the bodhisattva with skillful means postpones until his roots of merit are ripe for buddhahood.

literal: the reality-limit, the summit of the real

definitions.definition: The totality and true nature of dharmas; in the Avataṃsaka the boundless realm filled by Vairocana in which all worlds interpenetrate; synonym of suchness.
The true nature of things, which cannot be cognized by ordinary consciousness; the Buddha is to be seen from it; it abides whether or not buddhas appear.
That dharmas do not truly arise or cease; what is born from conditions is unborn by own-nature; non-arising, like suchness, neither comes nor goes and is the Tathāgata.

The bodhisattva's settled acceptance that dharmas are unborn and selfless, marking irreversibility; in the Daśabhūmika it is attained on the eighth ground; its merit surpasses gifts of jewel-filled worlds.

literal: acceptance (patience) of the non-arising of dharmas

cross_language.form: mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa

definitions.definition: The absence of intrinsic nature in dharmas; the Saṃdhinirmocana explains the sūtra statement 'all dharmas are without own-being' through three naturelessnesses.
Not finding or grasping any dharma as an object — the way the bodhisattva courses in the perfection of wisdom; rejoicing and dedication are done 'without apprehension'.
The standard simile of the Perfection of Wisdom: beings, dharmas, buddhahood and even nirvāṇa are like a magical illusion and a dream — appearing, yet without own-being.
That paired concepts — saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, defiled and pure, self and no-self — are not two; entry into non-duality is beyond words, shown by Vimalakīrti's silence.

equivalents.note: Both deny duality; the Mahāyāna sūtras deny a single substantial reality, while Advaita affirms Brahman; related by later polemics (dsp:advaita-crypto-buddhism)

definitions.definition: The three doors — emptiness (śūnyatā), the signless (animitta) and the wishless (apraṇihita) — which the bodhisattva cultivates, even in dreams, without realizing their fruit prematurely.

cross_language.form: rnam par thar pa'i sgo gsum
san jietuo men 三解脫門

definitions.definition: Grasping a composite (a world, a heap of atoms) as a real unity; the Vajracchedikā says it is inexpressible yet seized by common people.
The dharma as a raft to be left behind once the crossing is made — even dharmas must be abandoned, still more non-dharmas.

The full awakening of a buddha, the bodhisattva's goal; 'not even the least dharma is found in it — therefore it is called unsurpassed perfect awakening' (Vajracchedikā 22); all buddhas of the three times attain it by relying on the perfection of wisdom (Heart).

cross_language.form: bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub
anouduoluo sanmiao sanputi 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提

definitions.definition: Epithet of the bodhisattva: one armed with the great armor who has set out in the great vehicle to lead countless beings to nirvāṇa.
The bodhisattva's resolve to liberate all beings, 'put on' as armor, while knowing that there are no beings to be liberated.

The resolve to attain full buddhahood for the sake of all beings that makes one a bodhisattva; the Aṣṭasāhasrikā adds that the thought is 'no-thought', its nature luminous; the Avataṃsaka that at its first arising one already attains perfect awakening.
The path of those who aim at buddhahood for all beings, as distinct from the vehicles of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; also called great vehicle and buddha-vehicle.

cross_language.form: byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa

definitions.definition: The vehicle that carries all beings to full awakening; by its own account the Buddha's highest teaching, contrasted with the 'lesser' vehicle (hīnayāna) of those seeking personal nirvāṇa.
A polemical Mahāyāna term for the vehicles of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas when their goal is taken as final; not a self-designation of any school.

notes: Recorded as the Mahāyāna sūtras' own polemical usage; Theravāda does not use it of itself.

definitions.definition: The one vehicle leading to all-knowledge; in the Lotus the only vehicle, of which the three are skillful presentations.

The vehicles of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas and bodhisattvas; for the Lotus and Śrīmālā a skillful means leading to the one vehicle, for the Saṃdhinirmocana and Laṅkāvatāra matched to fixed lineages of beings.
The supreme vehicle for which the Vajracchedikā is taught, not hearable by those of low resolve.

The buddhas' and bodhisattvas' skill in adapting the teaching and their conduct to beings' capacities — teaching three vehicles for one, showing parinirvāṇa though the Buddha's life is immeasurable, living as a householder; joined with wisdom it keeps the bodhisattva from both saṃsāra and premature nirvāṇa.

cross_language.form: fangbian 方便 / shanqiao fangbian 善巧方便

equivalents.note: general Sanskrit 'means'; in Śaiva usage the four means (upāya) of practice

definitions.definition: The bodhisattva who can no longer turn back from full awakening, known by signs (Aṣṭa ch. 17); in the Pure Land sūtras those born in Sukhāvatī attain it.

cross_language.form: butuizhuan 不退轉 / abiba zhi 阿鞞跋致

definitions.definition: The teacher or companion who leads to awakening; the Aṣṭa says the buddhas and the perfections are the bodhisattva's good friends; Sudhana's pilgrimage and Sadāprarudita's search model devotion to them.
One who turns a new bodhisattva from the perfection of wisdom and makes him fearful.
Turning one's own and others' merit toward full awakening for all beings; supreme when done without apprehending merit, dedicator or goal.
Rejoicing in the merit of all buddhas, bodhisattvas and beings, itself productive of great merit.
Declaring one's evil deeds before the buddhas, with regret and resolve, to purify karma — as in the Golden Light's confession, the Triskandhaka and Samantabhadra's vows.
Mind (or giving) not resting on any object — form, sound, dharma — as the Tathāgata's mind stands nowhere; Kumārajīva: 'produce a mind that abides nowhere'.

cross_language.form: wuzhu 無住 / ying wu suo zhu er sheng qi xin 應無所住而生其心

definitions.definition: The buddhas' nirvāṇa that abides neither in saṃsāra (because of wisdom) nor in quiescence (because of compassion); prefigured in the sūtras' bodhisattva who neither destroys the conditioned nor dwells in the unconditioned.

cross_language.form: mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa

notes: The technical term is systematized in Yogācāra treatises (Mahāyānasaṃgraha); the idea is in the sūtras.

definitions.definition: Speech of the buddhas whose intent is hidden and hard to understand, fitted to beings' capacities.
The Tathāgata's knowledge and vision, which the buddhas appear in order to open, show, awaken and lead beings into.
The degeneracies of the aeon, of beings, of defilements, of views and of lifespan, in which buddhas teach the one vehicle as three.
In the Avataṃsaka the Buddha as he is seen in the dharmadhātu, his body filling all worlds; in the Brahmajāla sūtra the buddha on the lotus-throne.
One of the marks of a great man; the Buddha's ray from it lights up worlds before great teachings.

literal: the tuft (of hair) between the brows

definitions.definition: One who keeps, recites, explains and copies a sūtra; in the Lotus the Tathāgata's messenger.
A place of worship; in the Mahāyāna sūtras the spot where a sūtra is taught or kept becomes a caitya even without relics.
Honoring a written sūtra with flowers, incense, garlands and banners, held to exceed the worship of relics.
The final period ('last five hundred years') when the true dharma decays; the sūtras promise that some will still believe and keep them.

literal: the destruction of the true dharma

cross_language.form: fa miejin 法滅盡 / mofa 末法

definitions.definition: Obstacles Māra raises against the perfection of wisdom — distraction, weariness, doubts, preferring lesser sūtras, false visions of the Buddha.

The tempter who obstructs the bodhisattva; four Māras are named in Mahāyāna texts (of the aggregates, the defilements, death and the god-son Māra); in the Śūraṅgama demonic states arise from the aggregates.
A buddha's declaration that a being will become a buddha of a given name, land and aeon — Śāriputra as Padmaprabha, Śrīmālā as Samantaprabha, the Ganges goddess as Suvarṇapuṣpa.

notes: Separate from trm:vyakarana (grammar); if the merge keeps a single trm:vyakarana, this sense is the Buddhist one.

definitions.definition: The flesh eye, divine eye, wisdom eye, dharma eye and buddha eye, all possessed by the Tathāgata.
The samādhi of non-contention for which Subhūti is foremost; he does not think of himself as having attained it.
The unawakened who seize on self and on composites; 'foolish common people' are taught as no people.
One of the four notions (self, being, soul, person) whose presence disqualifies a bodhisattva.
The Buddha as the dharma / suchness, not his physical form: 'the guides have the dharma for body'; not sick, not fed by food; later the first of the three bodies.
The dharmakāya is the tathāgatagarbha freed from defilements; it is permanent, blissful, self and pure and pervades all beings.

equivalents.note: Pali DN 27 'Tathāgata has the dhamma as body' is an epithet; the Mahāyāna makes it a body of the Buddha

definitions.definition: The Buddha's visible body with the thirty-two marks, by which the Tathāgata is not truly to be seen.
The body in which the buddha, with the marks, teaches the Mahāyāna to bodhisattvas in pure fields; with the emanation body one of the two form-bodies arising from the dharmakāya.
The body that appears in the world, displays birth, awakening and parinirvāṇa to ripen beings.

cross_language.form: huashen 化身 / yingshen 應身

definitions.definition: The world-system a buddha teaches and purifies; pure fields such as Sukhāvatī and Abhirati exist in the ten directions; a field is pure as the bodhisattva's mind is pure.

cross_language.form: fotu 佛土 / focha 佛剎

definitions.definition: Amitābha's pure land in the west, created by his vows, where beings are born from lotuses and cannot retrogress; one reaches it by aspiration, merit and holding his name.

cross_language.form: jile 極樂 / anle 安樂

definitions.definition: Calling the Buddha to mind — his body, marks, qualities or name — leading to samādhi in which buddhas are seen; understood in the sūtras as mind-made and empty.

cross_language.form: sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa

definitions.definition: In the Chinese Pure Land sūtras, thinking of Amitābha or calling his name ('namo Amitābha Buddha'), even ten times, as the cause of birth in Sukhāvatī.

notes: Doctrinal development (Shandao, Hōnen, Shinran) belongs to U43.

definitions.definition: A power of retaining the teaching, and the formula that embodies it; dhāraṇīs protect preachers of the Lotus and are recited for merit and protection.

cross_language.form: tuoluoni 陀羅尼 / zongchi 總持

definitions.definition: oṃ maṇipadme hūṃ, the heart of Avalokiteśvara, first taught in the Kāraṇḍavyūha.

cross_language.form: liuzi daming zhou 六字大明咒

definitions.definition: The first letter, in which the whole perfection of wisdom is contained (Ekākṣarī PP).
The bodhisattva liberation by which Sumeru fits in a mustard seed without change to either.

cross_language.form: bukesiyi jietuo 不可思議解脫

definitions.definition: The samādhi of tenth-ground bodhisattvas containing all samādhis.
In the Śūraṅgama, complete penetration of reality through one entrance — a sense-object, faculty, consciousness or element; twenty-five are told.
In the Śūraṅgama the seeing-nature which does not move, age or perish, shown as the true mind.

notes: Distinct from Chan 'seeing the nature' (kenshō), though the same characters.

definitions.definition: The buddha present in every being, covered by adventitious defilements — the dharmakāya not yet freed; empty of stains, not empty of qualities; what saṃsāra and nirvāṇa depend on.
In the Laṅkāvatāra, taught to remove the fear of no-self and meaning emptiness, not a tīrthika self; identified with the ālayavijñāna.

literal: embryo / womb / matrix of the Tathāgata

cross_language.form: de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po

definitions.definition: The element or nature of buddhahood that all beings have (Chinese foxing); the Mahāparinirvāṇa says it is the meaning of 'self', the emptiness of the highest meaning and the middle way, and that even icchantikas have it.

cross_language.form: sangs rgyas kyi khams / bde gshegs snying po

definitions.definition: Said of all embodied beings for three reasons (RGV 1.27).
The spiritual lineage determining a being's vehicle: the Laṅkāvatāra lists five (śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, Tathāgata, indeterminate, none); Vimalakīrti calls the passions the Tathāgata's family.
The buddha-lineage present in all beings is one of the three reasons they are tathāgatagarbhas.

In the Laṅkāvatāra, one who has abandoned all roots of merit by rejecting the Mahāyāna — though the Tathāgata's power may revive his roots — or the bodhisattva who never enters nirvāṇa for beings' sake.
In the Mahāparinirvāṇa, first said to lack buddha-nature (in the sense of good qualities), then declared to have it and to be able to attain buddhahood; a fixed icchantika is denied.
The thought of awakening is no-thought, since the nature of thought is luminous (Aṣṭa 1).
The self-nature pure mind that is nonetheless defiled — hard to understand (Śrīmālā); the mind's nature rests on nothing, like space (RGV).

cross_language.form: sems kyi rang bzhin 'od gsal ba
zixing qingjing xin 自性清淨心

equivalents.note: the Pali luminous mind is not identified with a buddha-nature

definitions.definition: Defilements that are not the mind's nature but come to it like dust or clouds, separable from the tathāgatagarbha and removable.
The dharmakāya's perfections of permanence, bliss, self and purity, reversing the four inversions as applied to the Tathāgata.

cross_language.form: chang le wo jing 常樂我淨
gtsang bdag bde rtag gi pha rol tu phyin pa

definitions.definition: The subtle, beginningless ignorance that arhats and pratyekabuddhas have not removed; only buddhas remove it.
Neither increases nor decreases; identical with the tathāgatagarbha and the dharmakāya; the element when impure is called a being.
The Mahāparinirvāṇa's name for buddha-nature: an emptiness that sees both empty and non-empty, which is wisdom and the middle way.
The Tathāgata's knowledge, present within the host of beings (Avataṃsaka ch. 37; RGV 1.27).

cross_language.form: rulai zhihui 如來智慧 / fozhi 佛智

definitions.definition: The buddhas' spontaneous, uninterrupted activity for beings, illustrated by nine examples.
Awakening as the revelation of the stainless element when the stains are removed.
In the Saṃdhinirmocana the dharmakāya is the transformation of the basis.
Confidence in the supreme vehicle, the 'seed' of the buddha's children.
In the Awakening of Faith, the single reality with two aspects — suchness and arising-ceasing — identical with the tathāgatagarbha.
The mind's nature as already awake, the ground of non-awakening and actualized awakening (Awakening of Faith).
The consciousness that holds all seeds and the body, from which the other consciousnesses arise like waves from the ocean; in the Laṅkāvatāra identified with the tathāgatagarbha.

cross_language.form: kun gzhi rnam par shes pa
alaiye shi 阿賴耶識 / zangshi 藏識

definitions.definition: Name of the base-consciousness as appropriating the body; not taught to the foolish lest they take it for a self.

cross_language.form: len pa'i rnam par shes pa

definitions.definition: The sixth consciousness, cause and support of the others in the Laṅkāvatāra's account.

cross_language.form: yid kyi rnam par shes pa

definitions.definition: The seven consciousnesses that arise from the ālaya like waves.
'This triple world is mind only' (Daśabhūmika 6); the world is what is seen of one's own mind (Laṅkāvatāra); buddhas seen in samādhi are mind-made (Pratyutpanna).
The object of meditative consciousness is nothing but cognition (Saṃdhinirmocana ch. 8).
The Laṅkāvatāra's key term: all that appears is the perception of one's own mind; its stream is purified gradually and suddenly.

literal: what is seen as one's own mind

definitions.definition: The knowledge realized inwardly by the noble ones, beyond words and reasoning, the goal of the Laṅkāvatāra.

cross_language.form: so so rang rig pa'i ye shes

definitions.definition: Sign (nimitta), name (nāman), discrimination (vikalpa), right knowledge (samyagjñāna) and suchness (tathatā).
The imagined, dependent and perfected natures (the Saṃdhinirmocana's 'three characteristics').

cross_language.form: ngo bo nyid gsum / mtshan nyid gsum

definitions.definition: The nature of dharmas as designated by names and conventions — like hairs seen by one with cataract.
The suchness of dharmas, the object of the pure eye; ultimate naturelessness.
Naturelessness of characteristic, of arising and ultimate naturelessness — the intent of 'all dharmas lack own-being'.

cross_language.form: ngo bo nyid med pa gsum

definitions.definition: The Buddha's teaching as a turning wheel; the Saṃdhinirmocana distinguishes three turnings of differing definitiveness.
Teachings whose meaning must be drawn out further — for the Akṣayamati those speaking of self, being and the like; for the Saṃdhinirmocana the first two turnings.

literal: of provisional meaning (to be led on)

definitions.definition: Teachings whose meaning is final — for the Akṣayamati those teaching emptiness and no-self; for the Saṃdhinirmocana the third, well-distinguished turning.
The four reliances: on meaning not letter, dharma not person, gnosis not consciousness, definitive not provisional sūtras.
Two selflessnesses — of persons and of dharmas; the bodhisattva intent on 'dharmas are without self' is a bodhisattva.
The pair of meditations whose objects, stages and unity the Saṃdhinirmocana's eighth chapter explains.
Discerning examination of the image seen in samādhi as nothing but cognition.
The four analytical knowledges of dharmas, meanings, languages and eloquence, perfected on the ninth ground.
True seclusion as taught by Vimalakīrti: showing neither body nor mind in the three realms while acting in the world.
The attention whose single lamp-like act dispels karma and defilements gathered for aeons.

cross_language.form: tshul bzhin yid la byed pa

definitions.definition: Rests on the purity of mind and supports karma and defilements, as wind rests on space (RGV 1.55-57).
The first of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.
The second of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.
The third of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.
The fourth of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.
The fifth of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.
The sixth of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.
The seventh of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.
The eighth of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.
The ninth of the ten bodhisattva grounds in the Daśabhūmika.

One who has produced the thought of awakening and follows the path of the perfections to full buddhahood for all beings, refusing a merely personal nirvāṇa; yet 'no dharma called bodhisattva is found' (Aṣṭa 1).
'One who has not gone anywhere and has not come from anywhere' (Vajracchedikā 29); a synonym of true suchness; he knows the world's suchness through the perfection of wisdom.

For the bodhisattva not a final rest to be entered early: even nirvāṇa is like an illusion (Aṣṭa 2); the arhats' nirvāṇa is a resting place conjured by skillful means (Lotus 7); the Tathāgata's great nirvāṇa is permanent, blissful, self and pure (Mahāparinirvāṇa).
The single buddha-vehicle: the three vehicles are its skillful presentation (Lotus 2-3); the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha vehicles enter the great vehicle (Śrīmālā 5).

The perfection of wisdom that does not apprehend any dharma; it is the mother of the buddhas and leader of the perfections; wisdom without skillful means is bondage and means without wisdom is bondage (Vimalakīrti 4.16).

cross_language.form: banruo 般若 / zhihui 智慧

definitions.definition: The bodhisattva's six (giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom) or ten (adding skillful means, vow, power, knowledge) perfections, each perfected only when informed by the perfection of wisdom.

cross_language.form: boluomi 波羅蜜 / du 度

definitions.definition: The compassion that embraces all beings as an only child and from which the bodhisattva's illness arises; eating meat cuts off its seed.
The tenth bodhisattva ground, at which the bodhisattva is consecrated by the buddhas and rains the dharma like a cloud.
The ten grounds of the bodhisattva from Joyful to Cloud of Dharma, each with a predominant perfection.
In the Mahāparinirvāṇa and Aṅgulimālīya, the Tathāgata's true self, identified with the tathāgatagarbha, in contrast to the imagined self of the aggregates.
The bodhisattva's vows — Dharmākara's forty-eight, Bhaiṣajyaguru's twelve, Śrīmālā's ten, Samantabhadra's; the perfection of vow predominates on the eighth ground.
Compassion is the nurse of the buddha's children (RGV 1.34); love for beings seen as reflections and echoes (Vimalakīrti 6).
What dharmas are empty of: the Heart says the aggregates are empty of own-being.
Meditation on images without discrimination, paired with insight (Saṃdhinirmocana ch. 8).
The Heart Sūtra calls the perfection of wisdom the great mantra and gives gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā.
The third perfection, shown when the king of Kaliṅga cut the Buddha's limbs and he had no notion of self; also the 'acceptance' of dharmas' non-arising.
The first perfection, supreme when given without support in any thing.
In the Saṃdhinirmocana, the dependently arisen nature of dharmas, basis of the imagined.
The four inversions (taking the impermanent as permanent, etc.); the Mahāparinirvāṇa and Śrīmālā add a second set — taking the Tathāgata's permanence, bliss, self and purity as their opposites.
The sūtras deny the self of persons and dharmas (Vajracchedikā 25); the Mahāparinirvāṇa calls the tathāgatagarbha 'self'; the Laṅkāvatāra says this is not the self of the tīrthikas.
Seeing dependent origination is seeing the dharma and the Buddha (Śālistamba); what arises from conditions is unborn and empty (Anavatapta); the twelve links rest on mind (Daśabhūmika 6).

In the Lotus and Śrīmālā the arhat's nirvāṇa is not final — he still has the ground of ignorance and is destined for buddhahood; the Vajracchedikā: an arhat who thought 'I am an arhat' would seize a self.
The five aggregates, which Avalokiteśvara saw empty of own-being.
Without faith the roots are weak (Gaṇḍavyūha 55); faith in the buddha-element surpasses all other merit (RGV 5); faith in the vow brings birth in Sukhāvatī.
